subject: humanities
passage: When Johann Sebastian Bach died in 1750, his music was already considered old-fashioned, and for decades afterward it was known mainly to musicians, who studied his keyboard pieces as exercises. That began to change in March 1829, when the twenty-year-old composer Felix Mendelssohn conducted Bach's St. Matthew Passion in Berlin, the work's first performance since Bach's own time. The concert drew a large audience and was repeated within weeks. In the years that followed, interest in Bach's music spread across Europe, and many of his works were published for the first time.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Mendelssohn was the first musician to study Bach's keyboard pieces.
choices.B: Mendelssohn's performance helped revive wide interest in Bach's music.
choices.C: Bach's music was popular with large audiences throughout his own lifetime.
choices.D: The 1829 performance of the St. Matthew Passion drew a large audience.

explanation.why: The text first explains that after 1750 Bach's music was known "mainly to musicians." It then says "that began to change" with Mendelssohn's 1829 performance, after which interest "spread across Europe." The main idea is the role of that performance in reviving broad interest in Bach.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says musicians had studied Bach's keyboard pieces for decades before 1829.
explanation.B: Correct. This covers the whole text: Bach's music had faded from wide view, and Mendelssohn's performance began its revival.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says his music was considered old-fashioned by the time he died and never describes large audiences in his lifetime.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The large audience is one detail; the text's point is the wider revival that followed.
